Gaure Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tauragės apskritis, Lithuania

Demolished. Gaurė's small Jewish community, present from the 18th century, numbered only 17 residents by 1923, living simply on small farm plots. The village was the birthplace of Hebrew-Yiddish writer Nekhemya-Dov Hofman, whose 1916 memoir, published in Cape Town, South Africa, may have been the first Hebrew-Yiddish book ever published in that country. The remaining Jewish families of Gaurė were murdered in the Gryblaukis forest following the German-Soviet war's outbreak. This cemetery was destroyed during the Soviet era, with a school stadium built on the site, followed later by a culture hall and collective farm office.
